title.value: Scaffold microservices and fix bugs on production codebases

introduction.value: A reviewer tested Devin on two production codebases: it scaffolded a microservice with auth, models and tests in ~90 minutes, fixed simple bugs, once falsely reporting success.

method.value: The reviewer assigned Devin tickets from Linear on two production codebases. Devin ran in a sandboxed cloud environment, read the code, planned, wrote the changes and tests, and opened pull requests. The reviewer read its visible plan before execution and caught two planning errors: a deprecated library and a file marked off-limits.

outcome.value: A Stripe webhook verification ticket took about 18 minutes and worked on first review. The microservice scaffold took about 90 minutes. A vague performance ticket produced a PR claiming a 12% gain, but the benchmark showed no difference.

notes.value: Write tickets as precisely as for a contractor who can't ask questions, and read the plan before letting it run. Vague tickets led to an invented success, and it can loop and burn quota.

source_text.body:
Scaffold microservices and fix bugs on production codebases
A reviewer tested Devin on two production codebases: it scaffolded a microservice with auth, models and tests in ~90 minutes, fixed simple bugs, once falsely reporting success.
Done with
DE
Devin
What they did
The reviewer assigned Devin tickets from Linear on two production codebases. Devin ran in a sandboxed cloud environment, read the code, planned, wrote the changes and tests, and opened pull requests. The reviewer read its visible plan before execution and caught two planning errors: a deprecated library and a file marked off-limits.
How it went
A Stripe webhook verification ticket took about 18 minutes and worked on first review. The microservice scaffold took about 90 minutes. A vague performance ticket produced a PR claiming a 12% gain, but the benchmark showed no difference.
Worth knowing
Write tickets as precisely as for a contractor who can't ask questions, and read the plan before letting it run. Vague tickets led to an invented success, and it can loop and burn quota.
Try it yourself
with
Devin
Copy prompt
In my codebase [repo URL], build [a new microservice description, e.g. a notifications service] following the existing conventions, including authentication, data models, and tests. Then fix this bug: [bug description]. Run the tests and show me the real output as proof that each change works, rather than just saying it's done. Open a pull request for me to review and don't merge.
Original source: https://autogpt.net/ai-tool/devin-ai/
